key_insight: TACO proposes a memory-efficient optimizer for LLM fine-tuning that keeps closer to AdamW-like behavior while reducing optimizer-state overhead. It aims to preserve fine-tuning performance without needing the dense, memory-heavy states used by standard AdamW.
problem_solved: Full-parameter fine-tuning of large language models is often limited by optimizer state memory, which can prevent larger models from fitting on available GPUs. Existing compression or geometry-changing optimizers reduce memory but may hurt training quality or deviate from AdamW behavior.
method: Uses a ternary, absolute-max, column-wise, one-sparse update scheme to compress optimizer state.
Targets lower memory usage during fine-tuning while retaining an update style that is more compatible with AdamW-like optimization.
Aims to avoid the performance tradeoffs seen in approaches that substantially alter the optimizer geometry.
impact: For practitioners, this could make full-parameter fine-tuning of larger LLMs feasible on the same hardware budget. It may also offer a better balance between memory savings and training stability than prior memory-reduction methods.

paper_title: TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning
paper_authors: Jichao Jiang, Cristian McGee, El Houcine Bergou, Hanqin Cai, Aritra Dutta
